subsystems.name: Throat
subsystems.role: the narrowest part of the bridge, where spacetime is pinched and must stay open long enough to pass through.

subsystems.name: Exotic-matter source
subsystems.role: supplies the negative energy density that props the throat open against collapse.

subsystems.name: Stabilising ring lattice
subsystems.role: the arrangement of structures that shapes and holds the required negative-energy distribution.

subsystems.name: Mouth anchors
subsystems.role: keep the two ends of the bridge pinned to chosen locations rather than drifting.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal plant
subsystems.role: delivers the colossal energy the geometry demands and rejects the waste heat.

subsystems.name: Transit and shielding
subsystems.role: protects a spacecraft from tidal forces, radiation and vacuum effects inside the throat.

subsystems.name: Control and navigation
subsystems.role: monitors the geometry and steers the endpoints.

buildSteps.title: Solve the geometry
buildSteps.detail: General relativity gives equations for a traversable bridge (the Einstein–Rosen 1935 solution, extended by Morris and Thorne in 1988). One must first find a solution with acceptable tidal forces and transit time.

buildSteps.title: Determine the energy conditions
buildSteps.detail: Work out exactly how much negative energy density is needed, where it must sit, and for how long — the answer has always been 'more than any known process can supply'.

buildSteps.title: Produce negative energy at scale
buildSteps.detail: The Casimir effect demonstrates real negative energy density between close conducting plates, measured in the 1990s. The theoretical route is to engineer vacuum states — cavity geometries, moving mirrors — to amplify this from a microscopic effect into a macroscopic one.

buildSteps.title: Shape and hold the field
buildSteps.detail: A lattice of rings and coils would impose the required energy-density pattern on spacetime, with superconducting circuits maintaining it without resistive loss. No design for this exists.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the throat
buildSteps.detail: In principle the two mouths are created as a pair and the bridge between them stretched to the target separation, rather than 'drilled' through space.

buildSteps.title: Anchor the mouths
buildSteps.detail: Each end is fixed to a chosen point and held there against gravitational drift and the bridge's own tendency to pinch off.

buildSteps.title: Open for transit
buildSteps.detail: The throat is enlarged past the pinch-off threshold, pressures on the walls balanced, and radiation and tidal forces brought within limits a spacecraft can survive.

buildSteps.title: Operate and close
buildSteps.detail: Transit is monitored, the exotic-matter distribution adjusted in real time, and the bridge shut down to recover the energy invested.

prerequisites.why: the mathematics of traversable bridges is well developed on paper.

prerequisites.tech: Negative energy density from quantum vacuum effects
prerequisites.why: the Casimir effect is real and measured, but only at microscopic scale and tiny magnitude.
quantum inequalities appear to forbid the large, sustained negative energy densities a human-scale throat needs.

prerequisites.tech: Energy source of stellar or greater scale
prerequisites.why: even on paper, the energy and mass requirements dwarf anything humanity can currently command.
classical relativity breaks down where the throat pinches, and no tested theory of quantum gravity exists to describe that region.

pathway.milestone: theory only: wormhole solutions studied as mathematics, not engineering
pathway.unlocks: a precise statement of what would have to be true for one to exist.

pathway.milestone: laboratory quantum-vacuum experiments refining the limits on negative energy
pathway.unlocks: better bounds on what exotic-matter engineering could ever achieve.

pathway.milestone: a theory of quantum gravity that permits stable throats without unphysical matter
pathway.unlocks: a credible design target instead of an impossibility proof.

pathway.milestone: controlled production and shaping of macroscopic negative energy
pathway.unlocks: the first laboratory-scale, non-traversable geometry test.
interstellar transit measured in moments rather than millennia — if the physics allows it at all.
